name: Two-Peer Cross-Vendor Idea Fan-out
description: Generate ideas from two INDEPENDENT cross-vendor peers plus the host, then synthesise. Independence of failure modes is the point, not headcount: no peer ever sees another peer's output. The machinery that makes it work is a DISPATCH CONTRACT, because the measured failure was the adapter, not the vendor - three cross-vendor agents once produced zero artifacts while their coding quality was never exercised. So: the prompt travels BY FILE (an inline prompt blows the Windows command-line limit), the dispatch BLOCKS, and a result is accepted only on an AND-gate of exit code zero AND a non-empty output file AND a schema-valid parse. A result containing a background receipt string is rejected outright, and a repair loop retries an argument-limit failure exactly once with a scoped configuration before giving up terminally.

prompt.description: The idea-generation prompt; written to a FILE before dispatch

n_peers.description: At least two: one peer cannot be cross-checked for independence

peer_models.description: One entry per peer thread; distinct entries give model spread as well as vendor spread

output_schema_ref.description: The schema each peer result must validate against for the AND-gate to pass

dispatch_timeout_seconds.description: An explicit timeout is mandatory: the silent default is what a fire-and-forget dispatch was once rationalised to escape

prompt-marshaller.description: Writes the prompt to a FILE and records its byte count; an inline prompt above the OS command-line limit fails the dispatch outright

cross-vendor-peer.description: One fresh-context peer thread. Blocking dispatch, prompt by file, and NO sight of any sibling peer's output - that blindness is the independence being bought

dispatch-auditor.description: Applies the AND-gate: exit code zero AND a non-empty output file AND a schema-valid parse. Exit zero alone is SEVERED, not success

host-synthesiser.description: Merges the peer outputs and marks every idea that only ONE peer produced, because that is where the cross-vendor value shows up

routes.reason: the whole point is a vendor whose failure modes are not the host's

stages.title: Write the prompt to a FILE and record its byte count

work_unit.title: Marshal the prompt to a file, never inline, and record its size
work_unit.question_or_target: Write the prompt to a file under the artifact root and record its byte count and hash. An inline prompt above the OS command-line limit produces a hard argument-length error; the file route has no such ceiling.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: substantive subagents default to Opus (performance rule: quality over cost)

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the record carries the prompt file path, byte count and hash, plus the schema reference each peer must satisfy
tests_required: a prompt larger than the OS command-line limit must be handled by the file route and succeed, not fail with an argument-length error
the recorded byte count must match the file on disk
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the dispatch auditor reads the recorded hash and confirms every peer received the same prompt
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPB-0101 emitted only when the prompt file exists, is non-empty, and its recorded hash matches the bytes on disk; otherwise FAILED:BPB-0101 <failure-class> <reason>

stages.title: Dispatch the peers in parallel, BLOCKING, each blind to the others

work_unit.title: Run one fresh-context peer to completion and write its result to a file
work_unit.question_or_target: Dispatch one peer with the prompt file, a scoped configuration and an explicit timeout, and BLOCK until it finishes. Never background the call, never return a job id, and never treat a progress stream as a result. Write the peer's output to its own file.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a genuinely independent vendor: the value is uncorrelated failure modes, not extra headcount

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the dispatch record carries the exit code, the output file path, its byte count, and the elapsed wall-clock time - a turn count is not evidence a call blocked
tests_required: MANDATORY: a killed peer must produce a terminal FAILED marker with the diagnostic tail, never silence and never a job id
a result string containing a background receipt must be rejected by the auditor rather than parsed as ideas
the recorded wall-clock time must be consistent with a blocking call
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the dispatch auditor applies the AND-gate; this peer never self-certifies
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPB-0102 emitted only when the peer wrote a non-empty output file AND exited zero, or a terminal FAILED marker exists with its diagnostic tail; otherwise FAILED:BPB-0102 <failure-class> <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot: on an argument-limit failure retry ONCE with a scoped configuration, then fail terminally

stages.title: AND-gate every peer result: exit zero AND non-empty file AND schema-valid

work_unit.title: Compute the three-signal AND-gate per peer and classify every failure
work_unit.question_or_target: For each peer compute all three signals: exit code zero, a non-empty output file that exists, and a schema-valid parse. Only all three together are SUCCESS. Exit zero with no parseable file is SEVERED. Classify each failure into its taxonomy class.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: three mechanical checks; a model opinion about whether a dispatch succeeded is what let a progress stream be reported as an answer

work_unit.evidence_requirement: per peer: all three signal values individually plus the AND result and the failure class; an aggregate verdict without the three components is not the gate
tests_required: MANDATORY both-states: exit zero with an EMPTY output file must be SEVERED, and the same peer with a valid file must be SUCCESS
a result whose text matches a background-receipt pattern must be rejected outright
a schema-invalid but non-empty file must be schema-invalid, not SUCCESS
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the synthesiser consumes only peers this audit marked SUCCESS
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPB-0103 emitted only when every peer has all three signals recorded plus an AND verdict and, where failing, a taxonomy class; otherwise FAILED:BPB-0103 <failure-class> <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none: re-running a deterministic audit over unchanged files cannot change the verdict

stages.title: No peer result is accepted on exit code alone
Repair a failed dispatch once, with an INDEPENDENT verify

diagnose.title: Name the failure class from the audit, not from the stream

work_unit.title: Classify the dispatch failure from the recorded signals and state the root cause
work_unit.question_or_target: Read the audit and name the root cause per failed peer: an argument-limit failure, a severed stream, a non-zero exit, or a timeout. The taxonomy class determines the repair, so a guess here is a wasted retry.
work_unit.evidence_requirement: each diagnosis cites the recorded signal that established it (exit code, byte count, elapsed time, error text)
tests_required: an argument-limit failure must be distinguished from a severed stream: they take different repairs
a diagnosis with no citing signal must be rejected
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the verify gate is independent of this diagnosis and re-checks the AND-gate from scratch
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPB-0104 emitted only when every failed peer has a root cause citing the signal that established it; otherwise FAILED:BPB-0104 <failure-class> <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none: classification over unchanged records is deterministic

repair.title: Retry ONCE with a scoped configuration, per the diagnosed class

work_unit.title: Re-dispatch the failed peer once with the repair its class prescribes
work_unit.question_or_target: Re-dispatch each failed peer exactly once with the class-specific repair: an argument-limit failure gets a scoped configuration that drops the ambient tool inventory; a severed stream gets a fresh thread. Two strikes on the same fingerprint means stop, not try harder.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the repair is class-specific; a blind retry is what two-strikes forbids

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the retry records the repair applied, the new exit code, the new byte count and the elapsed time
tests_required: the retry must be attempted at most ONCE per peer - a third attempt on the same fingerprint is the anti-grind violation this bounds
a retry that fails again must produce a terminal FAILED marker, never silence
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the verify stage re-applies the full AND-gate; a retry does not self-certify
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPB-0105 emitted only when each failed peer has exactly one retry recorded, ending in SUCCESS or a terminal FAILED marker; otherwise FAILED:BPB-0105 <failure-class> <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: none at this level: the repair loop itself is the bounded retry, capped at two attempts

verify.title: Independent verify: re-apply the AND-gate from scratch

stages.title: No peer saw a sibling's output; every peer ended in a terminal state
Merge the peer ideas and mark what only ONE peer produced

work_unit.title: Emit merged ideas, disagreements, and the novel-to-one-peer set
work_unit.question_or_target: Merge the SUCCESS peer outputs plus the host's own ideas into three explicit sets: merged (more than one peer), disagreements, and novel-to-one-peer. The third set is where cross-vendor independence pays, so it is never folded into the first.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: substantive subagents default to Opus (performance rule: quality over cost)

work_unit.evidence_requirement: every idea names the peer or peers that produced it; the novel-to-one-peer set states which peer, so the independence value is measurable
tests_required: an idea produced by exactly one peer must appear in novel-to-one-peer, not in merged
if only one peer returned SUCCESS the synthesis must state the loss of independence explicitly rather than presenting one peer as consensus
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: one independent reviewer checks no idea in merged is attributed to a single peer
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BPB-0106 emitted only when the synthesis exists, parses, and every idea carries its peer attribution with the three sets kept separate; otherwise FAILED:BPB-0106 <failure-class> <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot: after two failures emit the raw peer outputs plus the blocking reason

impact.blast_radius: writes only under command-center/brainstorm/bp-brn-01/**; peers run in their own vendor sandbox with an explicitly set policy

derived_from.credit: owner (undeployed skill: the 2-peer fan-out and synthesis shape)
owner (the canonical scoped dispatch that keeps the call inside the OS argument limit)
measured: three cross-vendor agents produced ZERO artifacts because of the ADAPTER, not the vendor

contraindications: NOT when the answer needs repo grounding: the peers are fresh-context by design
NOT for a decision - that is a council
NOT when the question is already well-specified enough to just answer
x_extensions.the_measured_adapter_failure: Three cross-vendor agents once produced ZERO production artifacts against sixteen files, and the vendor's coding quality was never actually exercised - the failure was entirely in the ADAPTER. Hence: prompt by file (an inline prompt exceeded the OS command-line limit and killed both real attempts), blocking dispatch (a backgrounded job's result is unreachable because its record carries no session id), and an AND-gate (one agent forwarded a progress stream as its terminal answer while its own job record still read running).
unverified: UNVERIFIED post-repair; settling experiment = five dispatches requiring five non-empty schema-valid output files, and one deliberately oversized prompt that must succeed via the file route.

worked_example.name: two-peer idea fan-out on a harness design question

params.prompt: Enumerate mechanisms that would make an agent completion claim falsifiable without adding a new runtime.

acceptance: a prompt above the OS command-line limit succeeds via the file route
a killed peer produces a terminal FAILED marker, never silence
exit zero with an empty output file is SEVERED, not SUCCESS
an idea produced by exactly one peer lands in novel-to-one-peer

stopping_rule_controls.why: the floor keeps a single-peer run from reading as a completed two-peer fan-out
one surviving peer is not consensus and the run must say so rather than present it as agreement
